original_evidence.three_option_analysis_with_counterexampl: If the network is CONNECTED, a spanning tree has N−1 edges and the L−(N−1)=L−N+1 independent fundamental loops give B. A L+N−1 overcounts; C N−L+1 wrong sign generally. Stem only gives L ≠ N, not connectedness. For k connected components, number of independent loops is L−N+k, so e.g. L=4,N=4,k=2 gives 2 versus B=1 (here L=N, use e.g. L=5,N=4,k=2 gives 3 vs B=2; the counterexample must respect L ≠ N). The source model thus remains incomplete, not unconditional approval.

original_evidence.three_option_analysis_with_counterexampl: For normally motor-driven asynchronous machine n in [0,n_sync], slip s=(n_sync−n)/n_sync is 1 at standstill and approaches 0 near synchronous, so A intended. original_evidence.three_option_analysis_with_counterexampl: Typical feeder regulation uses transformer tap positions or shunt reactors/capacitors to modify voltage and reactive-flow, not a standalone resistor for economical network-wide voltage regulation, intended C. original_evidence.three_option_analysis_with_counterexampl: A current-limiting reactor is an in-series high-inductive-reactance element (X_L=2πfL) to increase fault-loop impedance, reducing short-circuit current: B large L. Reactor design may specify limiting X and transient recovery effects, not merely 'L mare' in isolation.
